title: Black hole as a multipartite entangler: multi-entropy in AdS3/CFT2
journal: Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics, 2026
topic: Worldline formalism / holographic transport / AdS-CFT tensor network
summary: Studies multipartite entanglement in BTZ black hole dual states using multi-entropy and Steiner tree geodesic networks. At high temperature, genuine tripartite multi-entropy shows volume-law scaling (vs size-independent in vacuum AdS3). Provides a new bulk geometric probe of multipartite entanglement structure.
key_findings: Genuine tripartite multi-entropy volume-law scaling at high temperature — new phase not seen in vacuum AdS
Steiner tree (minimal geodesic network) is the bulk dual of multi-entropy
Phase transition when one subsystem exceeds half the total: genuine tripartite entanglement vanishes
Radial cutoff dependence of multi-entropy gives nontrivial size dependence even for tripartite case
project_relevance: Tangentially relevant. The Steiner tree formalism is a generalization of the Ryu-Takayanagi geodesic that underlies our l_AdS measurements. If our MERA develops multipartite entanglement structure at finite temperature, the force profile could acquire corrections from non-minimal geodesic networks. Monitor for future relevance when we move to finite-temperature simulations.
